questions.q: Describe the different ways in which statistical data can be presented.
answer: Once data have been collected and organised, they can be presented in three main ways to make them clear and useful.

answer.text: In textual presentation the data are described in running paragraphs of text. This suits small sets of data and allows emphasis on particular figures, but it becomes clumsy and hard to follow when the data are large.

In tabular presentation, data are arranged in rows and columns in a statistical table with a title, captions for columns, stubs for rows, a body, and source and footnotes. Tables condense large data, allow easy comparison and form the basis for diagrams.

Here data are shown through diagrams and graphs such as bar diagrams, pie diagrams, histograms, frequency polygons and ogives. These give a quick and attractive visual impression and are easily understood, though they are less precise than tables.

answer: The choice of method depends on the nature of the data and the audience.
